stat_descriptions.avg_turret_output: Not a true average: this is the total damage output of all mounted turrets divided by 6 -- one for each direction along the 3 axes (+/-x, +/-y, +/-z). Real turrets cover wider arcs and can fire at different targets, so several directions can deal damage at once.
stat_descriptions.hull_damage_shielded_per_shot: Hull damage dealt on every hit even while the target's shields are up (shield bleed-through). This is the hull damage bonus; the base damage only reaches the hull once shields are down.
stat_descriptions.total_turret_output: This is not a game defined statistic, it sums all turret damage output across all fields of fire.
stat_descriptions.missile_max_speed: Confirmed against two real Encyclopedia entries: forward thrust divided by forward drag, the same terminal-velocity model a ship's own Max Speed uses.
stat_descriptions.missile_acceleration: The same F = ma model a ship's own Max Acceleration uses. Not independently confirmed against a real number, but built from the same trusted inputs as Max Speed.
stat_descriptions.missile_strafe_speed: Same thrust/drag model as Max Speed, on the strafe axis. 0 for every dumbfire missile (no strafing thrust at all -- it can't steer). Not confirmed against a real number.
stat_descriptions.missile_turn_rate_test: Test: the same thrust/drag model that correctly predicts a ship's own turning rate, applied to a missile. Confirmed WRONG -- the Heavy Guided Missile's real rate is 0.2°/s; this formula gives about 657°/s. Missiles most likely turn via a different mechanic (e.g. a seeker/guidance turn-rate limit) not present in the extracted data.
stat_descriptions.missile_max_distance: Max Speed x Time To Live -- the simplest possible distance estimate. Matches the Heavy Guided Missile's real range almost exactly (15.9 km), but undershoots the Heavy Cluster Rocket's real range by about 17% (8.2 km computed vs 9.8 km real) -- a missile needs time to accelerate up to top speed, so this simple model doesn't capture everything.
stat_descriptions.anomalous_range_multiplier: This range multiplier for dumbfire missile range is estimated from the game UI, the discrepancy is not known.
stat_descriptions.missile_game_value: These are values pulled from the game encyclopedia since I can't figure out a real accurate formula.
stat_descriptions.area_damage_per_shot: Damage dealt to everything within the blast radius, not just whatever this weapon directly hits -- shown alongside, not added to, its own direct per-shot damage (if it has any).
stat_descriptions.sustained_mechanism_r: Which Sustained DPS model this weapon uses, continuous or discrete heat generation, and that mechanism's own curve-fitted scaling constant (R).
stat_descriptions.sustained_fire_time: How long this weapon alone could fire continuously before overheating, used to derive Sustained Weapon Damage -- not the same figure as the in-game "Time to Overheat" tooltip for a beam weapon on a modified chassis (see Time to Overheat for that).
stat_descriptions.sustained_duty_cycle: The fraction of time this weapon spends actually firing once it settles into a steady fire/cooldown rhythm (Sustained Weapon Damage divided by Burst Weapon Damage).
stat_descriptions.sustained_dps: This weapon's own sustained output if it were the only weapon mounted -- fires, overheats, cools, and repeats indefinitely.
stat_descriptions.sustained_dps_ship_contribution: This weapon's own share of the ship-wide Sustained Weapon Damage total, accounting for every other mounted weapon sharing the same heat-cooldown pool.
stat_descriptions.ship_sustained_r_avg: The Sustained DPS scaling constant blended across every mounted weapon's own mechanism, weighted by how many of each are mounted.
stat_descriptions.ship_sustained_damage_total: The ship's total sustained weapon output with every mounted weapon firing, overheating, and cooling in rhythm together.
stat_descriptions.shield_bonus_groups: How many separate, individually-targetable hardpoint groups this chassis's own bonus shields are spread across -- not how many bonus shield slots exist (that's Bonus M Shield Slots), but how many distinct locations on the hull they're grouped into.
stat_descriptions.equipped_cost_avg: The sum of every actually-equipped component's own Avg Price, one per real slot -- engines, thrusters, shields, weapons, turrets, missiles, drones, deployables, countermeasures, crew, and software all added together. Mocking more of something than this ship really has slots for doesn't count the extras.
stat_descriptions.equipped_cost_min: The sum of every actually-equipped component's own Min Price, one per real slot -- engines, thrusters, shields, weapons, turrets, missiles, drones, deployables, countermeasures, crew, and software all added together. Mocking more of something than this ship really has slots for doesn't count the extras.
stat_descriptions.equipped_cost_max: The sum of every actually-equipped component's own Max Price, one per real slot -- engines, thrusters, shields, weapons, turrets, missiles, drones, deployables, countermeasures, crew, and software all added together. Mocking more of something than this ship really has slots for doesn't count the extras.

constant_descriptions.sustained_r_continuous: Curve-fitted scaling constant for the Sustained Weapon Damage formula on continuous-heat weapons (e.g. Pulse Laser, Beam Emitter).
constant_descriptions.sustained_r_discrete: Curve-fitted scaling constant for the Sustained Weapon Damage formula on discrete-heat weapons (e.g. Mass Driver).
constant_descriptions.turret_output_divisor: The game's own fixed divisor for Avg. Turret Output -- one per face of a cube a turret could fire from.

Use at your own risk. All names, trademarks, and content related to X4: Foundations are the property of Egosoft or their respective owners.
about.github_link_html: View this project on GitHub: https://github.com/lwhite12/x4-procurement-tool
about.built_from_hint: This site's ship/ware data is generated from these exact versions of the game and every installed DLC, alongside this tool's own version:
about.future_plans_hint: A few bigger features on the roadmap, not built yet:
about.user_accounts_body: Right now, sharing a fleet list, ship loadout, or price override preset means generating a one-off link (see the Share button above). The plan is to eventually add real user accounts, so you can save and recall your own fleet lists, ship loadouts, and price override presets directly -- without needing to keep track of links.
about.language_support_body: Ship and ware names/descriptions are currently only pulled from the game's English-language files. Support for reading other languages X4 itself supports is planned.
about.local_install_title: Running this locally against your own game install
about.local_install_hint: The hosted website covers the base game and all DLCs. The eventual goal of this is to run against a local install with any combination of DLCs/mods you want to use. However, this is untested so who knows if it works. If you want to try it, here's how:
about.local_install_step1_html: Clone the repository (see the GitHub link above) and install Python dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt.
about.local_install_step2_html: Obtain XRCatTool (an egosoft first-party X4 catalog-extraction tool -- not included in this repository) and place it at XTools_1.11/XRCatTool.exe under the repo root, or modify the repo code to point to your cli path. [link to the current XRCatTool download to be added here]
about.local_install_step3_html: Run python src/extract_game_data.py to pull ship/equipment/ware data out of your local X4 installation's .cat/.dat catalogs. By default this expects the game installed at C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\X4 Foundations -- edit GAME_ROOT at the top of that script if yours lives somewhere else.
about.local_install_step4_html: Run python src/generate_ships_table.py to build data/x4.db from the extracted files.

import_raw_xml_modal.hint_html: Paste a single <loadout ...>...</loadout> element, or a full <loadouts>...</loadouts> block containing several -- the same shape found in a saved loadouts.xml. Parsed ship loadout(s) are added to this app's own working set of imported loadouts (see "Select Filter Loadout") alongside anything already imported, rather than replacing it. This never writes to any file.
